contracts.authorization: Anonymous read-only GET. It grants no session, credential, configuration, payment or account authority.
contracts.idempotency: The query is read-only and returns an equivalent static declaration for repeated and concurrent requests.
contracts.compatibility: Version 1 is a closed response. New fields, capability names or schema versions require a new versioned contract before server and client changes.

inputSchema.description: No request body or query fields are accepted by the bootstrap declaration.

outputSchema.description: Closed desktop bootstrap recognition response v1.

success.description: Indicates that the static bootstrap declaration was returned successfully.

data.description: The complete closed desktop bootstrap declaration for contract version 1.

schema_version.description: The closed response schema version understood by the desktop client.

service.description: Stable service identifier used only for desktop bootstrap recognition.

contract_id.description: Stable identifier for this exact bootstrap contract.

minimum_client_version.description: Minimum desktop client version allowed to recognize this contract, expressed as strict three-part semantic versioning.

capabilities.description: Explicit capability declarations; every future integration remains disabled in this release unit.

device_authorization.description: Whether a governed device authorization flow is available.

account_read.description: Whether authenticated account projection is available.

usage_read.description: Whether account usage projection is available.

models_read.description: Whether the desktop model catalog contract is available.

pricing_read.description: Whether authoritative desktop pricing projection is available.

tool_keys_manage.description: Whether desktop tool-key management is available.

observability.correlation: No user or request correlation is emitted because this static anonymous query creates no operation.
observability.audit: No persistent audit record is created; normal HTTP access logging may record only the route and transport metadata under existing server policy.
observability.metrics: Existing generic route metrics may count requests; the contract exposes no customer or capability-use metric.

errorSemantics: Unsupported methods are not accepted and never change state.
The handler returns no secrets, account data, raw configuration or capability URLs.
Every future capability remains false until a separately governed implementation exists.
